candidateDecisions.rationale: Stable owners need a machine-readable contract for state, responsive, semantic, theme, and touch coverage.
Acyclic package ownership and core/advanced separation are architectural invariants.
Scatter, histogram, heatmap, grouped/diverging/normalized bars, multi-line, waterfall, range, bullet, and shared inspector mechanics are reusable but remain outside the minimal facade.
Critical information cannot depend on hover; a universal touch-safe tooltip needs a separate interaction contract.
No current cross-platform owner meets the complete keyboard/touch/native contract without a specialist adapter.
Virtualization, pinned columns, formulas, and cell editing are specialist infrastructure.
Low universal leverage and high dependency/platform cost.
Web and source contracts cannot prove physical device behavior.
Explicit help is already supported by the overlay contract without introducing a second positioning system.
Existing Button, ActionMenu, and shortcut composition cover the generic mechanics without a new public family.
Keyboard tree navigation and virtualization are valuable but materially more specialized than the core list/table contract.
Presentation can be composed without owning upload transport, file permissions, or a new media hierarchy.
The existing choice and multiselect contracts own the generic selection lifecycle.
The input needs platform capability selection and must not pull acquisition dependencies into the kernel.
ChartPanel, MetricTrendCard, BreakdownPanel, and flagship compositions repeat stable presentation anatomy while product meaning remains caller-owned.
Scales, finite data, deterministic ticks, shared state anatomy, and accessible table fallback are common mechanics.

Candlestick/OHLC, box plot, funnel, cohort, and combo composites remain intentionally deferred until concrete product demand supplies fixtures and interaction semantics; no vendor dependency is justified by the current reference app.
Selection, touch persistence, formatted multi-series context, stable IDs, and keyboard-safe fallback are shared mechanics used by advanced charts.
These require domain, platform, or heavy rendering infrastructure that Golden Base should not own.
